visual_idioms_needed: Rail-collapse idiom: parallel rails sharing src+dst (or leg_role+direction) get folded into a bundle node; the bundle must visually encode N (count), direction, and afford expansion-on-click to reveal individuals. Today the bundle just stacks the names vertically in the label — at N>=10 it overflows. Need a compact 'N rails' badge with on-hover or on-click expansion to a list/sidebar/popout.

XOR-group framing: nested sub-cluster inside a template cluster with a 'exactly 1 fires' contract label. Members are typically Variable-direction. The framing must (a) distinguish from the parent template's chrome (currently pale blue vs orange — works) AND (b) not get lost when the template cluster itself is dense.

Anchored-vs-bundled distinction: a rail is 'anchored' (rendered individually) if referenced by a chain or a template's leg_rails. Unanchored parallel rails collapse. The visual needs to make 'this is one of many' (bundle) vs 'this stands alone because it's load-bearing' (anchored) instantly readable — today both are identical ellipses, only the label differs.

Aggregating-rail decoration: aggregating rails (~2 in heavy) are sweep nodes with a cadence + an activity-ref list. Today INVISIBLE — needs a sweep glyph (clock/rhythm icon, or a 'sweeps N rails @ cadence' badge) AND optionally a ghost/dashed convergence visual from the bundled-activity rails into the sweep.

Direction-as-shape encoding (not just arrowheads): single-leg rails Debit vs Credit vs Variable should be readable from the rail node ITSELF, not just the edge it spawns. Variable direction (the XOR closing-leg case) has no special visual today; it's distinct posting-time semantic that operators need.

Origin-as-decoration: every rail (or leg) has an Origin (InternalInitiated / ExternalForcePosted / ExternalAggregated / custom). Today INVISIBLE in the diagram. Could be a small badge or border-stroke pattern on the rail node.

Cap-bearing role badge: roles that are LimitSchedule.parent_role need a cap badge (or stack of badges) on the role node, indicating direction (Outbound vs Inbound), cap magnitude, and target rail. Today only a label decoration on the control_parent edge.
Cap-subject rail tag: rails that appear in any LimitSchedule.rail field deserve a 'capped by N' indicator on the rail node so the operator sees 'this rail is throttled' without tracing edges.
Aging-watch indicator: rails with max_pending_age or max_unbundled_age set deserve a clock badge — they generate L1 exception views; today invisible.
Magnitude band: rails with amount_typical_range set have an implicit '$5 rail vs $5M rail' character; today invisible. Could be a thickness modulation on the rail node border or a $-icon scale.
Cadence band: rails with firings_typical_per_period set have a 'fires often vs rarely' character; today invisible.

Control-parent style distinct from chain style: today both are dashed gray edges, easy to confuse. Need clear visual separation between 'hierarchy / chart of accounts' (structural) and 'sequencing / firing rule' (behavioral).

Required vs XOR chain styling: chain rows with one child (required) vs multiple children (XOR) should look meaningfully different — operators scanning the diagram for 'where could a missing-fire exception come from' read these differently. Today only the label text disambiguates.

Fan-in chain emphasis: AB.6 fan-in edges already use penwidth=2.0 + double-arrow + label suffix; works but inconsistently 'emphasized' vs other chain decorations. Make this a deliberate idiom (e.g. 'funnel' glyph on the target).

Template-as-cluster vs template-as-port-node: the v13.1.1 audit's CF.3.f port-node proposal is the highest-payoff long-form change — each template becomes one Mrecord/HTML-table glyph with per-leg ports, edges dock at the exact leg, the entire template + its rails compress to one shape. The vocabulary needs to support either rendering with the same per-leg data-ids.

Focus dimming: when a node is focused (focus_node_id set), in-focus nodes are emitted, out-of-focus are skipped. The audit's CF.3.c proposal is 'fisheye': scale focus subgraph up, shrink everything else to label-less pins. Must use scale+opacity, NEVER display:none, so data-ids stay addressable for coverage/trainer tint.

Coverage tint: per-rail/per-template data coverage (X.4.c.5) stamps a tint over the node; the vocabulary must keep a 'tint surface' on every shape — the existing fill colors compete with this. Reserve a paintable region (e.g. left stripe or top bar) per shape kind.
Trainer-knob targeting: trainer mutations target specific entities; clicking a shape navigates to the editor. Every visible entity needs a stable data-id; bundle synthetic ids are a known gap.

Scope-perimeter framing: internal vs external roles divide the institution from counterparties. A higher-level visual (e.g. a soft envelope around all internal nodes, or a 'perimeter line' across the canvas) would let the operator see 'where does the institution end' at a glance.

Multi-role RoleExpression fan-out: when a rail has source_role=[A,B] and destination_role=[C], it currently fans into A→rail→C and B→rail→C edges via the cross-product. The visual must say 'this rail accepts any of these admissible roles' rather than 'this is three distinct rails'.

Cross-template rail sharing: Rail_23 in heavy is in BOTH TransferTemplate_01 AND TransferTemplate_13's leg_rails; current emit puts it in whichever template wins the seen_rail_ids race. The visual should either dual-cluster (rare, hard) OR flag the sharing.

Layer onion (L1 → L2 → L3): the layer parameter already gates rails+templates+chains by reveal level. The vocabulary must compose — shapes used at L3 must degrade gracefully at L1 (rails hidden) and L2 (templates+chains hidden). All elements must remain consistent in the data layer (so click-to-zoom on a role at L1 still produces the same role node at L3).

Stable identity across renders: bundle ids are deterministic from instance.rails iteration order (per :853-854 comment). The vocabulary mustn't introduce new synthetic ids that change between renders or between layers.

Density-graceful collapse: heavy_density_v1 has 158 nodes / 223 edges at L3 — every shape must remain at least small-readable at this scale. Per-shape information density is a real constraint (operator brief says 2-3 facts per shape minimum without label clutter). At smaller scales (sasquatch, 44 nodes), the same shapes should not look starved or over-decorated.
